# Input

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For one line of text: an email, a name, a search, a number. It is a native `<input>` with
the control look, so every native prop works and it ships no JavaScript.

```tsx
<label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
<Input id="email" name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" required />
<Input aria-label="Search" type="search" />
```

**A name is required.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`), `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`; the type refuses an Input with none of the three.

**`maxLength` has a default per `type`** (text 512, email 254, tel 32, url 2048, search and
password 256). Pass your own number, or `maxLength={null}` for no cap. Only those six types
take one, because HTML allows `maxlength` on no other: a `number`, a `date` or a `checkbox`
gets none, and a `number` is bounded by `min`, `max` and `step`. The case of `type` does not
matter, as in HTML: `type="Email"` is an email field.

**Its own width is `--tc-input-width`** (13.8em), and less in a narrow row, so two side by side
fit a phone. A grid or a column does not stretch it: pass `fullWidth` to fill, or your own `w-*`
class. `flex-1` grows past it.

**Beside a Button, put `flex-1` on the Input.** In a narrow row both shrink, so the Button's label
is cut while the field still has room. With `flex-1` the field takes only what the Button leaves.

```tsx
<div className="flex gap-2">
  <Input className="flex-1" type="email" aria-label="Invite by email" />
  <Button>Send invite</Button>
</div>
```

**`InputSkeleton` is the box of the field.** Give it the same `size` and `fullWidth`. It stands in
for a text field: for a date, a colour or a checkbox, pass your own `w-*` class.

```tsx
<InputSkeleton size="lg" fullWidth />
```

**Email, number, tel and url stay left-to-right** in a right-to-left form, on the form's side.
Pass `dir` to decide yourself.

**Text types only.** `checkbox`, `radio`, `range`, `color` and `file` render, but in the
text-field box, which is wrong for them: they belong to their own components.

**On a touch screen the text is at least 16px**, or iOS zooms the page on focus.
`size="custom"` opts out.

**A wrapper** takes `InputProps` and sets `type` inside. `Omit<InputProps, 'type'>` does not
compile: it merges the three ways to name an input into one where none is required.

**A parent that clips** (`overflow-hidden`) needs 4px of padding, or it cuts the focus ring off.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Input } from 'topclassui/input'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches the input to the width of its container. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid, and the border turns to danger and thickens. |
| `maxLength` | no | `number \| null` | - | The character cap: your number, the default of the `type`, or `null` for none. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The shared control scale; custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
